context: automation-commissioning-led · super-flat slab drives everything above it

brief.intro: An automated high-bay warehouse looks like a simple steel shed from outside, but the building exists to serve a machine: the automated storage and retrieval system (ASRS) that moves pallets or totes in and out of very tall racking around the clock, with no forklifts. The real programme driver is not the envelope — it is getting a dead-flat concrete floor down first, because ASRS cranes run on rails to tolerances an ordinary industrial slab cannot hold. From there, the automation contractor needs a clean, exclusive floor to erect racking, install cranes and conveyors, and commission the controls software that drives them. A late slab, or a floor still open to other trades, pushes the whole automation-commissioning window — and that window, not the roof, is what actually sets opening day.

scope.name: Enabling & earthworks
scope.desc: Site clearance, sub-base preparation, piling where required.

scope.name: Super-flat slab & foundations
scope.desc: Laser-screeded slab to a defined-movement-area tolerance, plus rack-post and crane-rail foundations.

scope.name: Structural steel / rack-clad structure
scope.desc: Portal frame, or a rack-supported (rack-clad) structure where the racking itself carries the roof.

scope.name: Building envelope
scope.desc: Cladding, roofing, dock doors, insulation — getting the shell weather-tight.

scope.name: Electrical power & containment
scope.desc: Power distribution to cranes and conveyors, containment and cable routes through the high-bay.

scope.name: Fire protection (ESFR)
scope.desc: In-rack and ceiling early-suppression fast-response sprinklers sized for storage height and commodity class.

scope.name: HVAC & building services
scope.desc: Warehouse ventilation/smoke-venting, plus office and mezzanine HVAC.

scope.name: Automation install (ASRS & conveyors)
scope.desc: Racking, storage/retrieval cranes or shuttles, conveyors and sortation equipment.

scope.name: Controls & WMS integration
scope.desc: PLC/WCS controls wired into the warehouse management system that decides where every load goes.

scope.name: Testing & commissioning
scope.desc: Equipment run-in, controls integration, a loaded throughput/duty test, fire-suppression sign-off and handover.

glossary.plain: automated cranes or shuttles that store and retrieve pallets or totes without a person driving.
the storage racking is itself the building's structural frame, carrying the roof and cladding.
the software that decides what goes where in the warehouse and instructs the automation.
the control layer that turns WMS orders into physical crane and conveyor moves.
early-suppression fast-response fire sprinklers sized for tall, dense storage.
an extra-flat floor spec that ASRS rail-cranes need in order to run smoothly.
running the automation continuously at target load and speed to prove it holds up in service.

must_get_right: Slab flatness is a procurement and programme decision, not a QA line item — the tolerance and laser-screed method must be locked before the floor is poured, because reworking a high-bay slab after racking starts is close to impossible.
Hand the slab over clean and exclusive — automation subcontractors cannot install racking or lay crane rails on a floor still carrying other trades' traffic or protection boards.
ESFR fire suppression is height- and commodity-specific and sits inside the commissioning chain, not before racking exists — it cannot be finally tested until the racking it protects is in place.
Reserve real time for controls integration and a duty/throughput test — racking and equipment being physically in place is not the same as the automation working reliably at target speed.

basis_of_planning.standard: AACE Recommended Practice 38R-06 — Documenting the Schedule Basis

sections.heading: Scheduling method & tools
sections.body: A Critical Path Method (CPM) network built in Primavera P6, developed to a Level 3 control schedule with retained-logic progress. Activities carry durations in working days; the network is calculated (F9) with no artificial constraints beyond contractual milestones. Total float is kept ≥ 0 in the baseline.

sections.heading: Calendars & working time
sections.body: Civil and structural steel run a 6-day week; the super-flat slab pour is scheduled as a continuous, weather-protected pour with no interruption once started; automation install and controls commissioning move to two shifts at peak to protect the throughput-test date.

sections.heading: Sequencing logic & critical path
sections.body: The driving path runs slab-tolerance sign-off → racking erection → crane/shuttle install & rail alignment → controls integration → duty/throughput test → handover. Structural steel and envelope are not on the critical path once the slab is handed over clean; automation install cannot start on a floor still open to other trades.

sections.heading: Key assumptions
sections.body: Rack layout, aisle widths and throughput targets are frozen before the slab is poured; the automation subcontractor's setting-out information is available in time to place rack-post foundations; a single, unobstructed mobilisation for automation plant; no change to storage height or commodity class after ESFR is designed.

sections.heading: Procurement & long-lead items
sections.body: The schedule is procurement-led on the automation equipment — tracked as milestones that drive the network:

rows: Before racking rises past first tier

sections.heading: Access, resource & site constraints
sections.body: The slab pour needs a large, uninterrupted weather window and a dedicated laser-screed crew; racking and automation installation need exclusive, clean access to the high-bay with no other trades working overhead; commissioning technicians for controls/WMS are a shared, specialist resource late in the programme.

sections.heading: Risks, float & contingency
sections.body: Principal risks: slab-flatness rework, automation-equipment delivery slippage, and controls/WMS integration re-work loops. Contingency is held immediately before the duty/throughput test and before handover, not spread across early civil activities.

sections.heading: Schedule levels of detail
sections.body: Reported at Level 1 (milestones) and Level 2 (summary) to the client; controlled at Level 3; expanded to Level 4–5 lookahead for the field — consistent with AACE 37R-06.
